reason: Psalmist recounts his own confession and addresses God; 'every holy one will pray' is a statement in prayer. Direction implied, not stated.

context: Same promise earlier in the psalm: evildoers soon vanish, while those who wait for the Lord and the meek inherit the land.
reason: Repeats existing coverage: 36:34 already promises that those who wait inherit the land as sinners perish; 36:11 is also linked to AUD-44-5-3.
Rhetorical question and accusation against unjust judges; no direction is stated, and the call to judge rightly is only implied.
5:11 continues the sentence of 5:8–10: the regret that follows ignoring the warning. Same speaker and charge, not a separate direction.
Folly's call ('turn aside to me') runs straight into her words at 9:17; join it to AUD-22-9-17, mirroring Wisdom's invitation 9:1–6.

title: Love of pleasure, wine and oil marks the needy man
speaker: Proverbial teacher (Solomon's proverbs)
reason: Only unrecorded proverb in chapter 21, where every saying is a Wisdom record. Title follows the Saints wording (the needy man loves pleasure).
23:27 ('for…') completes 23:26's sentence: keep my ways, for another's house is a leaking jar. Motive of the same charge, so extend.

title: The bloodthirsty hate the holy, but the upright care for his life
speaker: Proverbial teacher (Solomon's proverbs copied by Hezekiah's men)
reason: Only unrecorded proverb in chapter 29 apart from linked 29:17; a contrastive saying like its neighbours. Title glosses 'seek his life' as care.
Agur's confession of ignorance and rhetorical questions about the Creator: self-description and doctrine, with no direction; the call to humility is implied.

title: Like the leech’s daughters, Hades, desire and fire never say ‘Enough’
speaker: Agur, the man who speaks to those who trust in God
reason: Numerical saying on insatiable things, of the same kind as recorded 30:18–31; teaches the restlessness of desire. Title revised to the Saints list.
Heading and opening appeal of the same mother's instruction; 'keep God's sayings' comes as a question, so extend rather than create.

title: Oppression without a comforter makes the unborn more fortunate
speaker: Ecclesiastes (Qoheleth, the Teacher)
reason: Qoheleth's verdict on oppression, like published observations AUD-23-6-3 and AUD-23-8-9; the only unrecorded passage in chapter 4.
5:8 completes 5:7's reasoning about officials over officials, ending with the king and the land's yield. Same saying, not a new direction.
3:39's question (why grumble over one's sin?) leads straight into 'let us return'; same speaker and sense unit, not a separate direction.
Doctrine about the righteous dead's peace and immortality; no direction or conduct teaching. The review likewise trimmed the following 3:5–8 from AUD-26-3-5.
3:16 ('But…') is the antithesis of 3:13's beatitude: undefiled bed versus unlawful bed. Completes the same teaching rather than a separate record.
4:3 ('But…') completes 4:1–2's 'better' saying: virtuous childlessness against the rootless offspring of the ungodly. Same teaching, so extend.

context: Restates 4:7–9: the righteous who dies young 'fulfilled long years', and his early end condemns the unrighteous's long old age.
reason: Restates 4:7–9's teaching that honourable age is not length of years; not contiguous because AUD-26-4-10 (4:12) intervenes.
Statement within the prayer to God about the Egyptians' judgment after the plagues; narrative and doctrine, and the call to heed reproof is implied.
16:18–19 answer 16:17's quoted thought: heaven and earth shake when He looks on them, so none can hide. Same speaker, continuing passage.
19:5 opens the sentence that 19:6 completes ('…but the one who hates chatter'); 19:9 is already in the record, so add only 19:5.
Same adulteress as 23:22–23: her public judgment, rootless children and cursed memory complete the passage. Extending avoids a duplicate record.

title: Sirach’s sayings on a wife supporting her husband and an evil wife
speaker: Ben Sira
reason: Sayings on a wife's upkeep, an evil wife and sin's beginning, the kind published nearby (AUD-27-25-16, -19). Title revised to the Saints wording.
Continues 26:13–15's praise of a good wife (her beauty in an ordered house) with the same speaker; not a separate direction.
30:24 is already in the record; 30:25 closes the same saying on a glad heart that cares for its food.
The similes give the reason behind 32:3–4's 'do not hinder the music'; same banquet counsel and speaker.
32:10 gives the motive for 32:9's modesty: grace goes ahead of a modest person. Same counsel.
First half of the same comparison: as the Lord distinguished days, so people (33:8 and 33:11 match). Doctrine alone; extend, not a record.
35:19–23 is one sentence; AUD-27-35-23 now starts mid-sentence at 'until He judges'. Extend back to 35:19 and broaden its title.
37:14 ('For…') is the reason for 37:13's counsel to trust your own heart; same saying.
Continues 38:4–5 on medicines: God gave the knowledge by which He heals. Repeats existing coverage, so extend rather than a new record.
Craftsman, smith and potter continue the list begun with the farmer in 38:25–26 ('So also…'); part of the scribe-and-trades comparison.
Already linked: 39:16 is Additional Scripture on AUD-27-39-32. 39:17–18 praise God's word and command; they state or restate no direction.

context: The hymn's refrain again: nothing is hidden from Him, so none may ask 'What is this for?'; all things serve their uses.
reason: 39:21 repeats the refrain linked at 39:16 and restated in 39:34; 39:19–20 give its ground. Repeats existing coverage, so link.
39:26–27 continue 39:25 in AUD-27-39-22: life's necessities are good for the godly but turn evil for sinners. Same teaching.
Continues the same strophe (39:25 'evil things for sinners'): forces of retribution created to serve His command. Extend; not a separate teaching.
Continues 40:1–4's burden on all mortals: even sleep brings anxious dreams. Same passage and teaching.

context: Restates 39:25–30: death, sword, famine and scourge fall sevenfold on sinners, created against the lawless.
reason: Restates 39:25–30: calamities were created against the lawless. AUD-27-40-1 does not state this, so link rather than extend or duplicate.
Opens the same saying on death: 41:3 takes up 41:2's 'sentence' ('Do not fear death's sentence'). Same speaker and passage.
42:9–10 are already in the record; 42:13–14 ('For…') give the reason for 42:12's direction, so add only those.

title: Woe to the lawless, whose own works will come back on them
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah
reason: Divine woe on the lawless, like published Isaiah woes (AUD-28-5-8, AUD-28-10-1); 3:10's plot (ot-isaiah-v3-10) is the speech it condemns.
Woe oracle against Assyria and God's stated plan ('I will send… I will command'); no direction is addressed to anyone.

title: The ships of Carthage are told to wail over Tyre’s fall
speaker: the Lord through Isaiah (oracle concerning Tyre)
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
reason: Oracle imperatives (an inclusio at 23:1 and 23:14) to Carthage's ships; the catalogue records the parallel 23:6 and 23:10 imperatives.
'Announce to them' is the same charge to Isaiah that 30:8 continues ('Now then… write these things'). Same speaker and occasion.
32:6 ('For…') explains 32:5: the fool's lawless counsel against the devout's lasting plans. Continues that record; no separate direction.
45:21 continues the summons ('let them draw near so that they may know together'); same speaker and occasion.
Negative half of the same instruction: 'I did not choose this fast' (58:5) leads into 58:6's 'It is not such a fast.' Extend.
God's prediction of what He will do ('I will send… I will take'); no direction is addressed to the survivors or anyone else.

context: The Lord recalls having already told the dwelling of Israel, 'Return to Me,' before she was sent away.
reason: Recalled earlier call to the same addressee; 3:12 records 'Return to Me, dwelling of Israel'. Link as a recollection rather than a new record.

context: God's reply to Israel's confession restates the call conditionally: return, remove abominations, swear truly by the living Lord.
reason: Conditional promise with no imperative in the Saints text; it restates the call to return in God's reply to 3:22–25.
7:8 restates 7:4's warning against trusting false words; the sentence runs to 7:11's 'robbers' cave'. Same sermon and direction.
28:61 opens Jeremiah's charge to Seraiah that 28:62 continues ('and say'); consider retitling as that charge.
Continues the same instruction to Jeremiah: if the nations refuse the cup, say 'You will certainly drink.'
42:14 is the content of the message 42:13 sends Jeremiah to deliver: the Rechabites obeyed, Judah did not listen.
3:1 and 3:3 renew 2:8's command to eat; 2:9–10 and 3:2 are the connecting vision and fulfilment within the same passage.
21:19 renews the sign ('strike hand upon hand'); extended to 21:20 because the sentence ends there. Reference corrected from 21:18–19.
39:18–20 continue the same summons to birds and beasts ('you will eat… drink'); same speaker and occasion.
43:7–9 is one speech: Israel will no longer profane My name by prostitution and murder; 43:9 turns it into the direction.

title: The king hands Daniel over to destruction under the crowd’s pressure
speaker: the king of Babylon
recipient: his companions, before the hostile crowd
reason: Royal sentence handing Daniel to death, like the recorded order of Darius (AUD-31-6-15); spoken to his companions under the crowd's pressure.
Same occasion: the healing word 'be cleansed' precedes the charge; matches the linked Mark 1:40–45 and pericope practice (Luke 17:11–19).
